included: Current sourced Motherlode Mine access, tools, pay-dirt cleaning loop, capacity constraints, shop costs, output boundaries, interaction mechanics, and stop/re-entry mechanics.
A low-attention classification that is bounded by source-defined mechanical interruptions and does not represent a measured player-specific interaction interval.
excluded: Strategy, route order, account readiness, recommended 99 targets, reward purchase priority, world choice, and player-specific setup advice.
Guaranteed RNG, any hourly outcome, unattended safety, automatic activity completion, and inferred results from elapsed time.

source_catalog.use: Live mechanics source for entry and Mining gates, pickaxes, lower and upper vein windows, pay-dirt cleaning, sack and water-circuit state, rockfalls, logout/world-hop persistence, output boundaries, and reward access.
Live fixed nugget-shop stock, prices, resale values, and permanent Motherlode Mine upgrade costs.

Official historical confirmation that Poll 78 approved lower-floor Motherlode Mine vein-timer and additional-vein changes. It is not used to infer the current live values; those are taken from the checked live wiki page.

Historical official Project Rebalance skilling announcement URL checked for the 2024 Motherlode changes. It now resolves to an official 404 and is retained only to document the source-availability gap.

entry.claim: The area itself has no Mining-level entry requirement; 30 Mining, not boostable, is required to mine pay-dirt.

upper_level.claim: The upper level requires base 57 Mining, not boostable, and a one-time payment of 100 golden nuggets.

tools.claim: Any pickaxe can mine ore veins for pay-dirt; a pickaxe is also required to remove obstructing rockfalls.
Repairing a broken strut requires a hammer or Imcando hammer; nearby crates can provide a hammer, so ownership is not assumed.

locations.claim: The members-only Motherlode Mine is in the Dwarven Mine. A bank chest near Prospector Percy has no access requirement, but pay-dirt cannot be banked.
The upper floor is accessed by the ladder north of the bank chest after its one-time gate is met.

transport_options.claim: The dark tunnel by the bank chest requires 54 Agility and the Medium Falador Diary; a southern tunnel does not require the diary. No transport ownership or route is assumed.

inventory_inputs.claim: A usable pickaxe is the reusable tool for mining pay-dirt and clearing rockfalls.

bank_inputs.claim: The checked mechanics identify no bank withdrawal as a prerequisite; the nearby bank chest cannot store pay-dirt.

reusable_items.claim: A hammer or Imcando hammer is only needed when the player chooses to repair a broken strut; nearby crates are a possible local hammer source.

consumed_inputs.claim: The checked mine loop does not require a consumed item to mine, deposit, or search pay-dirt.

capacity_constraints.claim: Pay-dirt occupies inventory space and cannot be banked, so the current inventory count remains player-observed.
The standard sack holds 108 pay-dirt; the 200-nugget upgrade raises it to 189. At the applicable cap, the player cannot mine or deposit more pay-dirt until the sack is emptied below that cap.

classification_evidence.claim: The Wiki calls Motherlode Mine a low-intensity Mining training area. This package classifies the method as low_attention only because the loop has source-defined interruptions; it does not make an unattended-safety claim.

interaction_cadence.claim: A mined lower-level vein depletes 23-27 seconds after its first pay-dirt; an upper-level vein depletes after 36-40 seconds. These are vein lifetimes, not a promised player interaction interval.
The player must respond to a full inventory, the applicable sack cap, a depleted vein, an obstructing rockfall, or interrupted water flow before the relevant part of the loop can continue.
Actual click spacing, response time, mining success, and player attention tolerance are player-observed and are not calculated by this package.

session_mechanics.entry_condition: The player must reach the mine, meet the relevant Mining gate for the chosen floor, and have a usable pickaxe; exact location, supplies, unlock state, and current mine state remain reported rather than inferred.

duration_evidence.claim: No account-specific duration or output duration is modeled. The only relevant source-defined time ranges here are the lower and upper vein lifetimes.

session_end_events: A mechanical stop is reached when an actionable mine-loop boundary prevents the current step; detailed evidence is in session_end_event_evidence.

session_end_event_evidence.claim: At the current 108 or upgraded 189 sack cap, mining and hopper deposits are blocked until the sack is reduced below its cap.
When both struts are broken, pay-dirt in the circuit is frozen and newly deposited pay-dirt cannot reach the sack until the struts are repaired.
A depleted vein cannot continue yielding pay-dirt, and rockfalls can obstruct access until removed by a pickaxe or another source-defined actor.

repeatability_evidence.claim: The loop is mine pay-dirt, deposit it into a hopper, allow an operating water circuit to move it to the sack, search the sack, then continue or bank the collected ores. No repeat count is inferred.

offline_progression_evidence.claim: The source says pay-dirt circuit progress is saved through logout or a world hop; it does not describe progression continuing while the player is offline.

deterministic.description: The standard sack capacity is 108 pay-dirt and the permanent sack upgrade sets it to 189. Capacity is not a current sack balance.

Fixed-cost options are Prospector pieces for 40, 60, 50, and 30 nuggets; coal bag and gem bag for 100 each; soft clay pack for 10; bag full of gems for 40; upper level for 100 with 57 Mining; Super Hopper for 50 after upper-level access; and sack upgrade for 200. The 350 upgrade total and 730 all-unique-item-and-upgrade total are costs only, not targets or ownership claims.

A selected shop item or permanent upgrade has a fixed nugget cost once the player has an observed balance, meets its stated gate, and confirms the transaction; this package does not create either currency or ownership.

variable.description: Pay-dirt ore outcomes depend on Mining level, with better ores becoming more common at higher levels. The source says ore is determined when pay-dirt is mined, then collected after the pay-dirt reaches and is searched from the sack; no outcome count is inferred.
Each cleaned pay-dirt has a 3.13% golden-nugget chance regardless of Mining level. The actual nugget result is variable and must be observed when the sack is searched.

A strut repair succeeds by a Smithing-level-scaled per-tick chance, stated as 12% at Smithing 1 through 27% at Smithing 99. A repair attempt, success, and resulting Smithing experience are not inferred.

player_observed.description: Current pay-dirt inventory, hopper and in-transit pay-dirt, sack fill, strut condition, location, Mining and Smithing experience, and damage state are recorded only when supplied by the player.
Collected ores, golden nuggets, shop purchases, and permanent-unlock ownership are player-confirmed results, not outputs created from an activity selection or elapsed time.

damage_sources: Rockfalls can block paths and deal 1-4 damage to a player on the affected tile. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]

death_boundary.claim: The source documents rockfall damage but does not establish the player's current Hitpoints, supplies, recovery state, or death outcome; this package therefore leaves death_possible unknown.

logout_behavior: Pay-dirt progress in the water circuit is saved when logging out or hopping worlds. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
Strut state is world-specific, so a world hop can present a different strut condition without creating a result guarantee. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
safety_and_logout.safe_boundary: No unattended-safety conclusion is made. A player must recheck local mine state after any return before resuming actions.

safe_boundary_evidence.claim: This boundary follows the source-defined damage, path-obstruction, water-circuit, sack-capacity, and world-specific strut mechanics.

mechanical_stop_conditions: A vein depletes after its source-defined lower or upper lifetime and cannot keep yielding pay-dirt until it respawns. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
A full inventory prevents additional pay-dirt from being held; pay-dirt cannot be banked. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
At the 108 or 189 sack capacity, mining and depositing pay-dirt are blocked until the sack is below the applicable cap. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
When both water-wheel struts are broken, pay-dirt cannot move from the hopper to the sack until water flow is restored. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
A rockfall can obstruct an intended path until it is removed. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
mechanical_reentry_conditions: Resume mining only after the player has a usable pickaxe, can reach an available vein, and has capacity for the current loop state. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
Resume cleaning after pay-dirt is deposited and the water circuit can deliver it to the sack; the player must search the sack to collect results. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
After logout or a world hop, circuit progress persists but the player must observe the returned local state; strut condition is world-specific. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
reset_or_cleanup_requirements: Search and empty the sack below its cap before the blocked mining or deposit step can resume. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]

Restore water flow by successfully repairing struts with a hammer or Imcando hammer, or otherwise observe an operating circuit before expecting deposited pay-dirt to reach the sack. [wiki-motherlode-mine-2026-08-24]
There is no modeled global session reset; incomplete local state is reported rather than cleared by this package.

reconciliation.handling: Reference the existing action and minigame package only. This AFK package proposes no new or duplicate fact, action, node, edge, or observation ID. Any later amendment must preserve observation-only output and the documented capacity, water-circuit, RNG, and re-entry boundaries.

conflicts_and_unknowns.detail: The source supplies vein lifetimes and mechanical interruptions, but not a player-specific click interval or attention tolerance. No cadence beyond those source-defined windows is modeled.

The checked Wiki page describes an 8-second hopper-to-sack travel time, while its own change log says the depositing delay was removed in 2023. This package does not encode a deposit-duration value; only the water-circuit and sack-state boundaries are used.
Rockfall damage is sourced, but Hitpoints, food, recovery, player location, and resulting death risk are account state. They are not inferred.

The prior official Project Rebalance skilling-news URL returned an official 404 when checked on 2026-08-24. Poll 78 remains an official historical source, while the current live mechanics in this package are taken from the checked OSRS Wiki page.
